punchline: Zappos began without a warehouse, just photos of shoes sitting in someone else's store.
thirty_sec: Around 1999, Nick Swinmurn wanted to sell shoes online but had no idea whether people would buy shoes they couldn't try on. Instead of building warehouses and stocking inventory, he photographed a local store's shoes, posted them on a simple website, and bought each pair at full retail price when an order came in. People did order, which proved the demand was real. That company became Zappos, which Amazon later bought for roughly $1.2 billion.
question: If you had to prove your idea works without building any of it, what part would you do by hand first?
